title: Deleting a category moves work order lines but changes no price
refs: SV-11704 (Story 8 S8-R8 S8-E1 S8-E2),SV-11696 (Story 6 S6-R8),SV-12457 (Story 5 S5-R1)
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, on matrix A.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one range from $0.00 and Default on Markup % 50, pricing category A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on Default for work orders.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, with a part line of category A at a cost of $10.00 (sold at $15.00).
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer A, with the same kind of part line, invoiced.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings › Categories.
  2. Click category A's row.
  3. Open the page's three-dot menu.
  4. Click Delete.
  5. Click Delete in the dialog.
  6. Open work order 1.
  7. Open work order 2.
  8. Change the cost of work order 1's part line to 20.
  9. Click the Matrices tab on Settings › Pricing.
  10. Click the General Matrix's name.
  11. Type 20 in the Price Part Simulator's Part Cost.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Category A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Category A's page opens.

Step 3:

  • The menu lists Delete.

Step 4:

  • The delete question opens.

Step 5:

  • Category A is deleted.

Step 6:

  • Work order 1's part line shows category Uncategorized.
  • Its sell price still reads $15.00 ($10.00 × 1.50 = $15.00, priced by matrix A before the delete).

Step 7:

  • Work order 2's invoiced part line also shows Uncategorized.
  • Its sell price still reads $15.00.

Step 8:

  • Work order 1's line is repriced: its sell price changes from $15.00.
  • It does not read $30.00, matrix A's price for $20.00 ($20.00 × 1.50 = $30.00).

Step 9:

  • The Matrices list shows the General Matrix first.

Step 10:

  • The General Matrix's page opens.

Step 11:

  • Default's simulator price for $20.00 equals work order 1's new sell price (customer A is on Default).
